scope.target_workload: Qwen3-8B Q4_K_M on Apple M4 10-core Metal
scope.purpose: Classify historical AMD wins into target-neutral candidate concepts without transferring AMD ISA, route ids, wave assumptions, thresholds, or policy defaults.

classification_vocabulary.portable_concept: A semantic mechanism or candidate axis that can be expressed without an AMD backend assumption.
classification_vocabulary.compiler_work: A target compiler primitive must be demonstrated before the concept is executable or competitive.
classification_vocabulary.backend_specific_implementation: Historical implementation detail that is evidence for AMD only and must not be copied into Metal policy.
classification_vocabulary.irrelevant_first_metal_workload: The historical winning applicability does not match the first Qwen3-8B Metal workload; retain only as a later reopen concept.

metal_capability_vocabulary.observed: Measured on the exact Metal workload with identity-preserving evidence.
metal_capability_vocabulary.supported: The backend/compiler exposes the primitive, but the exact transferred route has not been measured.
metal_capability_vocabulary.unknown: Neither exact support nor competitive behavior is established by the pinned Metal evidence.

global_rules: AMD speedups establish historical applicability only; they are not Metal priors or performance promises.
Every Metal candidate must derive subgroup size, legal local size, address spaces, vector width, reduction form, and resource bounds from live target/compiler facts.
Semantic role, shape, quant, layout, dtypes, schedule, and replay grouping remain independent fields.
The ordinary tinygrad-generated Metal path is the control and fail-closed fallback for every row.
Only MR7 role-cost evidence may select rows for MR8; this matrix cannot promote or rank them.

rows.semantic_mechanism: At decode M=1, lanes cooperatively own contiguous packed Q4_K words for one output row, dequantize their owned words in registers, accumulate partials, and reduce the row across the subgroup. The portable idea is packed-word ownership plus a legal reduction, not the AMD G3 topology itself.

winning_workload.effect: Generated G3 was token-identical, route-clean, and within -0.13% to +0.41% of the owned AMD warp route at contexts 512, 1024, 2048, and 4096; the machine-authored policy conversion retained it as the generated default.

rows.semantic_mechanism: Replace one-row-per-thread serial Q6_K GEMV with cooperative K ownership: adjacent lanes read adjacent packed positions, emit per-lane partials, and reduce in a second generated stage. Route selection is role/shape-specific because split count and output size change the economics.

winning_workload.effect: The original cooperative path improved lm_head by 17.7-19.2% whole decode and ffn_down by 12.5-13.2%; the later spec-driven generated route was byte-identical to the shipped implementation across all three shapes, with worst generated/shipped timing ratio 1.0106 and 24/24 identical model tokens.

rows.semantic_mechanism: Use split-KV decode attention with online softmax state and a combine stage only in the context regime where its extra fixed work is amortized; retain ordinary SDPA below the measured crossover and select the graph per decode token rather than capture order.

winning_workload.effect: On AMD, flash regressed at contexts 128 and 256, crossed near 384, and increasingly won through 4096. The conservative shipped cutover moved from 1024 to 512 after a byte-identical +12.8% real-generate result near ctx520; a later generate fix ensured sessions that start short actually switch graphs at the threshold.

rows.semantic_mechanism: Treat attention locality as an explicit candidate axis: stage K in local memory while reading V through a measured warm-cache path, reducing local-memory footprint and staging instructions. The choice is valid only when producer/consumer cache residency and resource evidence support it.

winning_workload.effect: The generated UOp K_ONLY route halved local memory from 8192 to 4096 bytes, removed the V staging loop, and improved AMD whole decode by 7.8% at ctx512 and 14.7% at ctx2048. The original K+V G=5 block tile had previously regressed about 80%, so the locality axis—not the G=5 grouping alone—was decisive.
